newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sets major sell-offs for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia sets major sell-offs for 1997.

text.p: Russia's Federal Property Fund will sell 15 percent of Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil this year, a senior fund official said on Thursday.
The fund will also sell a stake of 1.5-2.0 percent in national power company Unified Energy System (UES) after around six months, fund Deputy Chairman Vladimir Malin said.
Large stakes in Russian-Belarussian joint venture Slavneft, an oil group whose main operating company is Megionneftegaz, will also be sold this year, he told a news conference.
Malin said plans to sell off 34 percent of oil group ONAKO, whose main operating company is Orenburgneft, had been put off until 1998 at the request of authorities in the region where it is based.
But he confirmed the fund intended to sell 50 percent of Russia's biggest insurance company Rosgosstrakh this year.
In addition to the 15 percent stake in OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil, the fund is also considering selling an option on 4.5 percent of the company, he said.
"We cannot yet say when (the 15 percent stake) will be sold, but it is in our plans for this year," he said.
"We are preparing documents for selling an option on LUKoil shares, but it must still be agreed with the Federal Commission for the Securities Market," he added.

The 1.5-2.0 percent stake in RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) comprises shares left over from a previous cash auction of shares in the company and from the employees' fund in the company.
The exact timing of the sale would depend on market conditions, he said.
Shares in Slavneft will be sold both at a special cash auction and an investment tender.
The auction, of two percent of Slavneft from Russia's stake in the venture, will be held in both Russia and Belarus, Malin said.
But he was not able to say how much of Slavneft would be sold altogether, because of the group's ownership structure, but it would be less than 34 percent.
